give me a detailed explanation of james webb
a: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) is the largest and most powerful space telescope ever built, launched on December 25, 2021. It observes the universe primarily in infrared wavelengths, allowing it to see through dust clouds and observe the earliest galaxies, stars, and planetary systems. Unlike the Hubble Space Telescope which observes mainly in visible and ultraviolet light, JWST's infrared capabilities let it detect redshifted light from the universe's first galaxies, peer into stellar nurseries obscured by dust, and analyze the atmospheres of exoplanets. It orbits the Sun at the second Lagrange point (L2), about 1.5 million kilometers from Earth, keeping it in a stable position with minimal heat interference. Its primary mirror is 6.5 meters in diameter, made of 18 gold-coated beryllium segments that unfolded in space. A five-layer sunshield the size of a tennis court protects it from solar radiation. Key discoveries include unprecedented images of the Carina Nebula, Stephan's Quintet, and SMACS 0723 (the deepest infrared image of the universe), as well as detections of carbon dioxide in exoplanet atmospheres and complex organic molecules in star-forming regions.

q: metallic taste in mouth when cut
a: The metallic taste people experience when bleeding or when blood contacts their tongue is primarily due to the iron content in blood. Hemoglobin, the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen, contains iron atoms at its core. When blood comes into contact with taste buds on the tongue, the iron ions (particularly Fe2+ and Fe3+) interact with taste receptors, triggering a metallic taste sensation. This is the same mechanism that makes iron supplements and certain multivitamins taste metallic. Human blood typically contains about 450 to 500 milligrams of iron per liter. The phenomenon also involves lipid oxidation in blood, which produces compounds similar to those that give metal its characteristic taste when touched. Interestingly, the metallic taste of blood is so distinctive that many predators are attracted to it, which is why small amounts of blood can signal injury to animals. The sensitivity to the metallic taste of blood varies between individuals and can be influenced by genetic factors.
